title: Self-Reflective Claim Verification for Scientific Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Standard RAG models blindly condition LLM generation on retrieved passages without verifying whether retrieved text logically entails intermediate premises. We propose a self-reflective reasoning framework that performs step-by-step claim decomposition and natural language inference over retrieved passages prior to synthesis. Our method reduces hallucinated citations to under 2% while boosting reasoning accuracy on GSM8K and MMLU.

sections.Abstract: Standard RAG models blindly condition LLM generation on retrieved passages without verifying whether retrieved text logically entails intermediate premises. We propose a self-reflective reasoning framework that performs step-by-step claim decomposition and natural language inference over retrieved passages prior to synthesis. Our method reduces hallucinated citations to under 2% while boosting reasoning accuracy on GSM8K and MMLU.
sections.Introduction: Hallucination in language model reasoning remains a primary bottleneck for scientific adoption. While retrieval provides grounded facts, language models frequently hallucinate relationships not supported by the cited excerpts.
sections.Methodology: We integrate NLI verification directly into the decoding loop, verifying entailment of each generated clause against retrieved chunks.
sections.Experiments: Evaluated on GSM8K reasoning benchmarks and scientific subsets of MMLU across Mistral and LLaMA backbones.
sections.Results: Verification improves Citation Faithfulness to 96.4% and raises reasoning accuracy on MMLU scientific subsets to 82.5%, compared to 71.2% for naive retrieval.
sections.Conclusion: Explicit claim-level verification is essential to ensure retrieved evidence is authentically reflected in scientific generation.
